描述_ZN: A blue and white lily-wrapped double-ringed ear vase, Ming Yongle, 46 cm high, 7 cm in diameter, 35 cm in back.　　The vase has a straight mouth and short neck, with a raised neck with a one-week string pattern, decorated on one side with a small tie. The vase is flattened and unglazed on one side, with the center recessed like an umbilicus, and raised on the other side, with the center protruding like a hemisphere, with a live ring ear on each side of the shoulder. The entire body is decorated in blue and white, with the mouth rim decorated with a wrap-around flower, the raised abdomen decorated with an octagonal brocade pattern of seawater and river cliffs, the interior painted with a wrap-around flower, its periphery decorated with a wrap-around flower, and the sides of the bottle decorated with a seawater and river cliffs pattern. The blue and white colors are rich and lustrous, and the decoration is smooth and natural, with a strong sense of movement.　　This vessel is unique in shape, large in size and resembling a turtle, and was fired under the influence of West Asian culture to imitate the shape of Arabian bronze vessels, also known as "reclining pots".
